entities.name: House of Plantagenet
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The House of Plantagenet, a dynasty of English kings who ruled from 1154 to 1485, was founded when Henry II ascended the English throne following the Anarchy (civil war between Stephen and Matilda), inheriting through his mother Empress Matilda and ruling vast territories from Ireland to the Pyrenees in what historians call the 'Angevin Empire.' During their 331-year reign, the Plantagenets produced some of England's most consequential monarchs — Richard I (Lionheart), John (who sealed Magna Carta 1215), Henry III, Edward I (Hammer of the Scots), Edward III, and the Black Prince — and fundamentally shaped English constitutional, legal, and cultural development.

The dynasty's defining achievements: Magna Carta (1215, under John) established that no one — including the king — was above the law; Edward I's Model Parliament (1295) established the principle of parliamentary consent for taxation; the reign of Edward III inaugurated the Hundred Years' War (1337-1453) with France and established English common law courts. Henry II's legal reforms (1166 Assize of Clarendon, 1176 Assize of Northampton) created the common law jury system that influenced all English-speaking legal systems.

The dynasty's later period — the Lancaster-York conflict (Wars of the Roses, 1455-1485) — saw the Plantagenet line fracture between the House of Lancaster (red rose, descended from John of Gaunt) and the House of York (white rose), ending when Henry Tudor (a Lancastrian) defeated Richard III at Bosworth Field 1485, founding the Tudor dynasty. The Plantagenet legacy persists in Magna Carta's influence on the US Constitution and the English common law tradition across the global common law world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The House of Plantagenet — producing Magna Carta (foundation of constitutional law), the English common law system (governing 30% of the world's population), and parliamentary government — is one of history's most constitutionally consequential dynasties, directly shaping the US Constitution and Anglo-American legal civilization.
